gaps.sentence: She would rather ___ at home tonight.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather do' — the bare infinitive follows.

gaps.sentence: I remembered ___ the door, so I went back to check.
gaps.explanation: remember + -ing = recall a past action; remember to do = not forget a duty.

gaps.sentence: I'm sorry for ___ so long to reply.
I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.

gaps.sentence: After introducing herself, she went on ___ the main findings.
gaps.hint: move on to a new activity
gaps.explanation: go on + to-infinitive = do something after finishing something else.

gaps.sentence: He continued ___ as if nothing had happened.
gaps.explanation: continue takes -ing or to-infinitive. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: We stopped ___ something to eat at the motorway services.
gaps.explanation: 'Stopped to get' = paused for the purpose; 'stopped getting' would mean quit eating.
